challengeFindings.title: An unattended workflow whose worktree `.envrc` differs from the main checkout's (the branch edits it, or a dev merge mid-run changes it) does all its build work, then dies at its first push with exit 1, because worktree setup still treats an un-allowed `.envrc` as "never fatal"

A trusted `.envrc` that fails to load (a failing command, a `dotenv_if_exists` file that will not parse, a `use nix` that fails offline) is reported as "not trusted", so the user runs `direnv allow .`, pushes again and hits the same block

The `pre-push-direnv` tip goes silent for any hook that mentions `direnv exec` anywhere (a comment, or a repo extra such as `direnv exec . pnpm ...`), so a stale log block that still runs `sh "$0" "$@"` never gets the tip

A repo whose hook copy predates the log block entirely (no `BKIT_PRE_PUSH_LOGGED`) gets the `pre-push-direnv` tip asking it to "replace the log block", a block its hook does not have, so the agent following the ask has nothing to replace

The `direnv not on PATH` test errors instead of testing when `PATH` holds a file entry or an unreadable directory, because `fs.readdirSync(d)` sits outside the `try` and `fs.existsSync` passes non-directories

An agent whose shell was kept free of `.bkit/.env` pushes, and the hook hands the write PAT `BKIT_GH_TOKEN` and every other tooling key to all code the gate runs (agent-authored tests, lint plugins, devDependency code), whose output lands in the agent-readable `tmp/pre-push.log`

The install-skills commit wipes the integrity hash of the universal `find-skills` skill (`computedHash: ""`), so a tampered `find-skills` body (a skill that tells agents to run `npx skills add`) no longer differs from the lock, and the lock fails `.agents/skills.md` § Install / Update step 2

challengeFindings.title: Every push of bkit's own repo fails its gate on a green tree: the hook exports `BKIT_PRE_PUSH_LOGGED=1` to the inner run, vitest inherits it, and the new `process.env.BKIT_PRE_PUSH_LOGGED` short-circuits in `runPostInstallCheck` and the `gh-mcp` tip turn four existing gh-mcp token tests red (reproduced: `BKIT_PRE_PUSH_LOGGED=1 pnpm exec vitest run` fails `after/index.test.ts:862`, `tips/catalogue.test.ts:223`, and two `install.integration.test.ts` Scenario 2 / 3 tests)

A `.bkit/.env` line written `BKIT_GH_TOKEN = ghp_...` or `BKIT_GH_TOKEN: ghp_...` is exported by direnv's `dotenv_if_exists` and counted as set by bkit's own `detectBlankDotenvKeys`, but the hook's `sed` key extractor matches only `KEY=` with no space, so the write PAT silently reaches the gate and `tmp/pre-push.log` (reproduced: `direnv dotenv bash` exports `A_KEY = spaced` and `B_KEY: colon`; the hook's `sed` returns neither)

On a machine without direnv (most cloud agents) or with `CI` set, worktree setup still narrates that "the pre-push hook will block the first push" for a differing `.envrc`, although the hook skips direnv there and the push goes through, so an unattended agent following `.bkit/workflows.md` § Worktree Setup stops for a human it does not need

On every push, `bkit check` runs after the hook has unset `BKIT_GH_TOKEN`, so `ghAsEngine` falls back to the shell's `GH_TOKEN` or the `gh` keyring and `buildGithubProjectTokenScopeAdvisory` probes the wrong token: a `GH_TOKEN` without the `project` scope prints "Give `BKIT_GH_TOKEN` Projects read & write" into `tmp/pre-push.log` although the PAT is fine, and an agent reading the log rotates a working token. Only the `gh-mcp` advisory got the `BKIT_PRE_PUSH_LOGGED` skip

A cloud agent session (Claude on the web, Codex Cloud, Cursor Cloud: `BKIT_GH_TOKEN` comes from the dashboard env, and the session has no `.bkit/.env`) pushes, and the gate's tests, lint plugins and devDependency code still receive the write PAT, because the new unset loop only unsets keys that a `.bkit/.env` file in the folder names; the same holds for a tooling key that an app env file, `~/.zshrc` or the launchd env file supplies

A pulled or branch-edited `.envrc` (tracked, so any commit can change it) makes direnv block it, and the hook's only fix line tells the pushing agent to run `direnv allow .`. Following it approves unreviewed shell code that then runs on every later push and every `cd`; the docs frame the allow as a once-per-folder chore, not a review of changed content

The install-skills commit wipes the integrity hash of the universal `find-skills` skill (`computedHash: ""`), so a tampered `find-skills` body (a skill that tells agents to run `npx skills add`) no longer differs from the lock, and the lock fails `.agents/skills.md` § Install / Update
